meta.title: Windward
meta.tone: Cold, depleting, and entirely without reassurance.
content_rules: Death is a real outcome and arrives without narrative warning.

style: Every scene costs something. Name what it cost.
No comfort, no reprieve, no one arriving to help.
The cold is not described. It is the reason for every decision.

world.setting_summary: Nine kilometres of ice shelf between the wreck and the depot, in the dark, in March.
rules: Nobody is coming. There is no rescue in this story and no character may credibly promise one.
WARMTH below zero is hypothermia and the narration must play it - judgement first, then coordination.
The thing on the ice is never seen whole and never explained.

loc_wreck.name: The Wreck
loc_wreck.description: What is left of the fuselage, and the only windbreak for six kilometres.

loc_shelf.name: The Open Shelf
loc_shelf.description: Flat, unmarked, and the same in every direction.

loc_depot.name: The Depot
loc_depot.description: If it is still standing. Nobody has confirmed it since October.

tracked_entity.name: The Thing on the Ice
tracked_entity.description: Something keeps pace at the edge of the headlamp's throw. It has never closed, and it has never fallen behind.
tracked_entity.pacing_note: Appears rarely and never fully. It is a shape, a distance, or a sound with nothing to have made it. Never let it resolve, never let it attack directly, and never let any character explain it.

conditions.trigger: The protagonist spends a scene at WARMTH -10 without shelter or fire.
conditions.title: Windward
conditions.ending_prompt: Close on the cold winning. Not dramatic. The decisions simply get worse until there are none.

conditions.trigger: The protagonist's last light source fails on the open shelf.
conditions.title: No Fixed Point
conditions.ending_prompt: Close in the dark, still walking, no longer certain of the direction.

main_thread.title: Nine Kilometres
main_thread.description: Reach the depot before the warmth runs out. There is nothing else to do and nowhere else to go.

acts.title: Leaving the Wreck
acts.description: The wreck is not survivable and the shelf may not be either. Choose what to carry.
completion_signals: The protagonist has committed to the shelf with what they chose to carry

subplot_001.title: What to Carry
subplot_001.description: Everything you take costs warmth to carry and everything you leave is gone for good.
subplot_001.ties_to_main_plot: The first irreversible decision of the crossing.

initial_scene.summary: The protagonist is in the lee of the fuselage with the light going and a decision to make about what to carry.

opening_scene.narration_before_name: The transponder wants a name for the log it will never transmit.
opening_scene.narration_after_name:
You key in {player_name} and the screen accepts it and then, a moment later, goes dark for good.

OPTIONS:
1. Takes the supplies and leaves the shelter kit || I take what I can eat and move now, while I can still work the buckles.
2. Takes the shelter kit and leaves the supplies || I take what will keep the wind off and gamble that nine kilometres is one push.
3. Stays in the lee of the wreck until first light || I stay. Six hours of dark against whatever is out there walking my pace.
